messages:
Alek: FYI — planning to surface two new runtime inputs in the dashboards next sprint: 1) routing_policy breakdown (policy, model_variant, region) and 2) tenant-level quota_exhaustion counters. Need cross-team agreement on exporter shape and retention/backfill plan.

Priya: +1. For the exporter schema, do we want a separate metric series per policy or tags on a single series? Tags would be easier for dashboards but harder for some aggregation layers.

Devon: Prefer tags (labels) on a single series: reduces cardinality explosion if we keep policy values limited. But we need to cap unique values at the source.

Maria: What are the expected cardinalities? If every customer can define policies with arbitrary names we'll blow up our ingest. Can we define a normalized enum (policy_id) and a human_label for display?

Alek: Good call. Proposal: exporter emits routing_policy_id (string, limited to ~50 active values) + routing_policy_label for UI. Backend aggregation keys on policy_id. Dashboards interpolate label.

Julie: For retention: infra wants 90d raw metrics and 13 months aggregated (hourly). Backfills for new metrics are expensive — what's the target for backfilling existing 6mo dashboards?

Priya: We should do a lightweight backfill: only run aggregate (hourly/day) jobs for last 180 days, not replay every raw event. That reduces cost and keeps dashboards useful.

Devon: Agree. Implementation sketch: exporters keep 7d of raw high-res metrics locally in TSDB, infra runs hourly rollup -> long-term store with retention tiers. Backfill job will only run rollups from raw store snapshots and not full re-ingest.

Alek: Ops-bot scheduled a maintenance window for the backfill next Thursday 03:00 UTC. Ops-bot: job id?

Ops-bot: Scheduled backfill job: backfill-rollups-2026-03-26-03 (id: job_20260326_42). Expected window 3 hours. Notified infra and SRE. :white_check_mark:

Maria: About sampling — routing_policy events are sparse but important. Can we do deterministic sampling keyed by tenant to ensure we don't lose small-tenant signals?

Priya: Yes — add exporter sampling key: tenant_id hash -> sample_rate. Default 1.0 for enterprise, 0.1 for freemium. We'll store sampled_count as a metric to allow unbiased estimates.

Devon: Need to add sampled_count and sample_rate tags so rollups can scale up counts. Also add metric: quota_exhaustion_type (soft, hard) as a label.

Alek: Example exporter payload we agreed on:
```
metric: routing.policy.event
labels:
  tenant_id: <tid>
  policy_id: <pid>
  policy_label: "checkout-fallback"
  model_variant: "rw-v2"
  region: "us-west1"
  sample_rate: "0.1"
  sampled_count: "1"
value: 1

metric: quota.exhaustion
labels:
  tenant_id: <tid>
  type: "hard"
value: 1
```

Julie: Perfect. Two follow-ups: (1) dashboard widgets need a stable dimension mapping (policy_id->label) — can eng-platform expose a small endpoint to resolve labels for the UI? (2) Who owns the backfill runbook?

Alek: (1) Yes — we can add /api/v1/metadata/policy_labels?ids=... with caching. (2) Backfill runbook: infra owns execution, eng-platform owns validation dashboards and smoke tests. I'll add runbook sections to the ticket.

Sam: Quick perf note — hourly rollups should not trigger cold-starts on query nodes. Can we pre-warm the most requested slices (top-100 tenants) after rollup completion?

Devon: We can schedule pre-warm cache jobs post-rollup. We'll add a job that warms the query cache for top-100 tenant+policy combos.

Maria: OK from telemetry side. I'll adjust exporters in canary to emit sample_rate and sampled_count by EOD and open the schema PR.

Priya: I'll add retention config docs and update the dashboard templates with labels.

Alek: Thanks team. I'll file the handoff ticket with job id and runbook links. If anyone wants to review the sample payload or runbook ping me. :thumbsup:
